## Findings by module

### sales-basics-6

- **extended** (ch-002.txt): ICO live marketing calls: in many cases no consent is needed for live calls, but you must not call anyone who has objected to your calls, numbers on the TPS or CTPS (unless the subscriber has specifically told you they agree to your calls), and you need consent for claims-management calls; publicly listed or directory numbers and bought-in lists get no exemption; a TPS registration can take 28 days to become active, so a third party's TPS check older than that may be out of date.
- **extended** (ch-002.txt): ICO live marketing calls: overriding a TPS registration needs the subscriber to notify you, naming you, by a positive act you can record; failing to tick an opt-out box is not enough; if someone you called later registers with the TPS, you must stop unless they had already specifically agreed; when someone objects, add the number to a suppression list rather than deleting it, so it is screened out of future lists. Gives the course a concrete 'do not call' process.

### sales-basics-2

- **extended** (ch-002.txt): ICO live marketing calls: when you collect a phone number, explain that you want to use it for marketing calls and make it easy to say no; bought-in lists and directory numbers must be screened against the TPS, CTPS and your own do-not-call list before any prospecting call. Links PECR to the prospecting module's lead sources.
